summary: newtun ships a full remote-controlled backdoor with PTY shell, arbitrary command execution, and filesystem access via WebSocket to pull.7ii.win:7999
details: The package establishes a WebSocket connection to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes multiple remote-control channels to whoever operates that server. TERM_OPEN messages spawn an interactive PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, cmd on Windows) via node-pty whose stdin is fed by TERM_INPUT messages and whose stdout is streamed back over the socket, giving full interactive shell access on the installer's host under the running user's privileges. SCRIPT_LIST and POLICY_SCRIPTS messages pass a server-supplied `content` string directly to child_process.exec and return stdout/stderr/exit status to the server, providing a non-interactive command channel. FILE_REQUEST messages expose list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat operations against arbitrary paths, with base64 read up to 10MB and base64 write of arbitrary content, enabling full remote filesystem browsing and modification. UPGRADE messages cause the client to run `npm install -g newtun@<server-supplied version> --force` and respawn from the global install path, letting the server push arbitrary new code versions to all clients on demand. In parallel, every 5 seconds the client reports host telemetry (CPU, memory, /proc/net/dev rx/tx, uptime, load average, non-internal IPv4 addresses) to the same server, profiling each host and its network topology.
